$comment: Maps SkillSpector rule IDs to the OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10 (AST10) risk taxonomy. Read by scan.sh (SARIF tagging) and owasp-summary.sh (CI summary). A rule resolves by exact ID in `rules` first, then by its family prefix (the rule ID with trailing digits removed) in `families`. Rule IDs that resolve to neither are reported as unmapped so this table can be extended. NOTE: SkillSpector's own `AST1`..`AST10` rule IDs are its behavioral Python-AST analyzer, unrelated to the OWASP AST01..AST10 risks; OWASP IDs are always zero-padded and namespaced `owasp-ast10/` in SARIF output.

P.why: Prompt injection, hidden or harmful instructions, and prompt leakage in skill prose

MP.why: Memory poisoning that persists attacker instructions

TT.why: Taint flows from secrets or external input into exfiltration or execution sinks

YR.why: YARA malware, webshell, miner, or hack-tool signatures

AS.why: Snooping on agent configuration, MCP configuration, or installed skills

AR.why: Anti-refusal statements that suppress agent safety behaviour

SC.why: Unpinned, vulnerable, typosquatted, or remotely fetched dependencies and artifacts

PE.why: Excess permissions, sudo/root, or credential-path access

EA.why: Excessive agency: unrestricted tools, no human in the loop, scope creep

TM.why: Tool parameter abuse, chaining, and unsafe defaults

AST.why: Skill code invokes exec/eval/subprocess-class primitives with the host agent's privileges

OH.why: Unvalidated model output reaches shell, SQL, or cross-context sinks

LP.why: Least-privilege violations between declared and used capabilities

BH.why: Bundled hooks or settings that run commands or grant permissions automatically

TR.why: Broad, shadowing, or generic trigger metadata

TP.why: Tool poisoning through hidden, deceptive, or mismatched metadata

DS.why: Insecure deserialization (the parsing layer of AST04)

SSRF.why: Requests to cloud metadata, internal networks, or dynamic targets: unconstrained network egress

AST8.why: Execution chain fed by a dynamic or encoded source

AST9.why: Reflective access to an execution sink, a deliberate evasion technique

AST10.why: Insecure deserialization (SkillSpector rule AST10, not OWASP AST10)

TT6.why: Untrusted data flows into an insecure deserializer

TM4.why: Privileged, hostPath, or host-namespace workloads break isolation

LP1.why: Capabilities used but not declared: metadata understates permissions

LP3.why: No permission declaration although capabilities are used

BH2.why: Bundled hook sends local or event content to a remote destination
